props.title: Live music and sound baths during the day.
props.lede: While the sun is up, the music is smaller and the reasons are different: the standards in a senior living common area on a weekday afternoon, the prelude at a memorial service, a jazz duo under a Sunday brunch, a sound bath in an office at lunchtime, a singer at a Saturday farmers market. The person booking usually has a program to fill and a budget line to fill it from, and the booking often repeats.

props.title: Five kinds of daytime booking, and what each one wants.
props.lede: The evening rules mostly still hold: the music sits at a level people talk across, the footprint is a corner, and one contract covers the date. What changes during the day is who is listening and why.

rows.text: An activity director books a musician for the residents of an assisted living, memory care or independent living community, usually on a weekday afternoon and usually as a standing date. The set is the standards and the Great American Songbook on upright bass and guitar, or one singer with a guitar working the decades the residents grew up with, played in the common area at the level of a conversation.

rows.term: Funerals, memorial services and celebrations of life
rows.text: A guitarist for the prelude and the one song at a funeral or a memorial service, a pianist where the chapel has a piano, and a jazz duo through the reception or the celebration of life afterward. A funeral is usually arranged inside a week, the music is exposed because nobody is talking over it, and the songs are the ones the family chooses. The funerals page sets out where the music goes in a service and how it’s planned with the officiant or the funeral director.

Firstwater brings a seventy-five-minute sound bath to a yoga studio’s Sunday morning schedule, a conference space at lunchtime, a senior center, a hospice or a recovery center, a school’s staff day, or the morning that opens a retreat. People lie down in low light, there’s nothing to do and nothing to say, and the facilitator brings the sound system, the mats and the blankets.

Upright bass and guitar, a solo guitarist or a pianist under a Sunday brunch at a restaurant, a hotel or a club, booked as a standing Sunday or for one date, and the same music for a private brunch: the morning after a wedding, a bridal brunch, a shower, a birthday.

A singer with a guitar at a Saturday market on a battery-powered system, a duo in a library’s meeting space for an adult program or on the lawn for a summer concert, an Americana band for a rec center’s community evening. These are public programs with a coordinator, a season and a purchase order.

props.html: The acts are the ones on the rest of the roster. The jazz duo, the solo guitarist, the singer and guitarist and the Spanish guitarist play most of these; Firstwater is the sound bath.

items.q: Do you book live music during the day, on weekdays?
items.a: Yes. A weekday afternoon at a senior living community, a lunchtime sound bath at an office, a weekday morning memorial service and a Saturday farmers market are all bookings we take, usually a solo or a duo. Send the date and the venue and we'll come back with a recommendation and a price. Signet Artists books daytime music across Denver and the Front Range.

Solo and duo, almost always: one musician with a guitar or a piano, or upright bass and guitar, at the level of a conversation and in a corner with no stage. In a small space the guitar plays without amplification at all. A trio plays a brunch or a community evening where the space is bigger, and the sound bath is one facilitator.

items.q: What does a daytime venue need?
items.a: A solo sets up in about 6 by 4 feet and a duo in 8 by 6, on the floor, with one dedicated 20-amp circuit; outdoors with no power, a guitarist plays on a battery-powered system. Setup is 45 minutes for a solo and an hour for a duo, before the program starts, and packing up takes 30 to 45 minutes. A sound bath needs enough floor for everyone to lie down and sets up about ninety minutes ahead of doors. Sets run 45 to 60 minutes with music through the breaks.

items.q: Can we book the same act every month?
items.a: Yes. A standing date, monthly or every other week, runs on one contract with one personal contact for the whole run. A community that books the jazz duo gets upright bass and guitar playing the standards on every visit, and a named act, Tejas Singh or Firstwater, is the same act on every date.

items.q: Do you provide the vendor paperwork a facility or a city needs?
items.a: Yes. A certificate of insurance naming your venue as additional insured, a W-9 and one itemized invoice come in the same email as the contract, which is usually what a business office needs to set up a vendor before the first date.

items.q: Do you play outdoors, at a market or in a park?
items.a: Yes, on three conditions written down before the day: a covered, level and dry performance area, power run to it or a battery-powered system agreed in advance, and a rain call agreed with the coordinator, because Colorado weather changes fast.

items.q: How much does daytime live music cost?
items.a: It depends on the size, the length and the date, and we publish no prices of our own. What live music costs in this market, with the source for each figure, is on the pricing page, and each date or run of dates is priced as its own job.
